title: Bounded below complexes embed quasi-isomorphically into complexes of injectives
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives, let $a\in\mathbf Z$ and let $K^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $\mathcal A$ (indexed by $\mathbf Z$) with $K^n=0$ for $n<a$. Then there exist a cochain complex $I^\bullet$ of $\mathcal A$ whose terms $I^n$ are injective objects [def-sp-injective-resolutions], with $I^n=0$ for $n<a$, and a morphism of complexes $\alpha:K^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ such that every $\alpha^n:K^n\to I^n$ is a monomorphism and $\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism, i.e. $H^n(\alpha):H^n(K^\bullet)\to H^n(I^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 013K (lemma-injective-resolutions-exist, line 6280), part (3); Stacks proves (3) as a special case of Lemma Tag 05T6 (lemma-subcategory-right-resolution, line 5387)

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-subcategory-right-resolution-05T6] with $\mathcal I$ the subset of injective objects of $\mathcal A$. The zero object is injective (the unique map out of zero gives the required extension), and the enough-injectives hypothesis says that every object is a subobject of an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Therefore Tag 05T6(1) supplies a quasi-isomorphism $\alpha:K^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ whose terms $I^n$ are injective, whose degree maps $K^n\to I^n$ are monomorphisms, and with $I^n=0$ for $n<a$, exactly the asserted conclusion.
